question: Does the global trait-average difference act as a graded prior, such that larger leave-one-family-out trait-mean separation predicts more stable pairwise ordering inside a lineage?
predictor: absolute difference between the two trait means estimated from all other families
outcome: 1 if the focal family's observed trait ordering matches the leave-one-family-out predicted ordering, 0 otherwise; ties excluded
summaries: agreement by quartile of absolute prior margin
Spearman association between absolute margin and agreement
linear-probability slope per 1 SD margin with two-way clustering by family and trait pair
interpretation: A positive margin-agreement relationship means trait averages behave as probabilistic priors: strongly separated traits are more likely to preserve order, while weakly separated traits are readily re-ranked.
role: post-outcome explanatory analysis only; cannot rescue the failed prospective AusTraits rank-portability criterion
hard_nonclaims: Do not call a positive calibration relationship a universal hierarchy.
Do not interpret nonmonotonic quartile bins as contradiction if the continuous clustered slope remains positive.
Do not use the analysis to redefine trait pairs or thresholds.
